entries.detail: Grades routing choices for an exported production query log and writes a CSV report. It has no pass/fail contract at all -- it throws on a missing input and otherwise emits grades -- so there is no verdict for the harness to collect. Its DEFAULT_FILE is an absolute path into a developer's Downloads directory for an export that is not in the repository, so it cannot run offline in a clean checkout, and DEFAULT_OUT writes into audit/. Discovered only because the rule matches `test` as a MIDDLE basename segment; the four globs revision 1 proposed would all have missed it.

Post-deploy smoke checks against a running deployment. Since the credential containment increment a bare invocation resolves http://localhost:3000 and production must be named explicitly, but either way it requires a live server, so it cannot be a default-run offline correctness command. Retries before failing, which is right for a smoke check and wrong for a deterministic test.

Explanation-quality suite that needs a live endpoint AND grades model output, so two independent reasons put it outside the deterministic chain: it contacts a deployment, and the same input can legitimately produce a different answer on the next run. Registering it would make the correctness verdict depend on a model sample.

Stress tool: generates roughly a hundred natural-language queries with Claude, runs them against a live API, and flags anything over a ten-second wall-clock threshold, writing reports to scripts/eval/results/. Non-deterministic input, a timing threshold, report output, and a network dependency -- four separate reasons it is a diagnostic rather than a correctness test. The only nested candidate recursion found beneath scripts/; a top-level-only scan would have missed it entirely.

A genuine offline correctness test -- 15 sessions, 71 steps of multi-turn routing over lib/tab-suggest -- that is RED today, and is quarantined rather than registered, deleted, or quietly edited. Three failures with the hate-crime flag on, two with it off. One is a demonstrably stale expectation: `hate crimes in New York City since 2019` expects nibrs, from before hate_crime was routable, and it disappears when the flag is off, which is what proves it is the flag. The other two are flag-independent -- a Baltimore/DC chart comparison and a rape-clearance share, both classified as follow-ups where the test expects a fresh route -- and deciding whether the router or the follow-up semantics is wrong is a product judgement. Registering it as-is would turn the suite red inside an accounting increment; deleting it would discard 68 passing steps; editing the expectations would answer the product question by fiat.
entries.follow_up: Bounded decision increment: rule on the two flag-independent follow-up disagreements (Baltimore/DC chart comparison, rape-clearance share) -- router defect or stale follow-up semantics -- then correct the one stale hate_crime expectation and register this file as Tier F, removing this entry. Blocked on the product judgement, not on harness work.

entries.detail: Required offline test of the builder's --maintenance-window exception (receipt, lock owner and phase, PM2 state, settled source, fixed production paths). It needs Linux: fcntl.flock for the maintenance lock and the server's shell stubs. Run by .github/workflows/linux-release-build.yml, step "Server-maintenance tests", as the runner user and as root, under Python 3.12.3.

Required offline test of the updater's population stage, settlement and publication, server-rollup stage, attempt-process disposition and restart decision. It needs Linux: fcntl.flock, /proc process scans and process sessions. Run as root by .github/workflows/linux-release-build.yml, step "Server-maintenance tests", under Python 3.12.3.

Required offline test of the maintenance lock and its descriptor inheritance. It needs Linux: fcntl.flock and inherited file descriptors. Run by .github/workflows/linux-release-build.yml, step "Server-maintenance tests", as the runner user and as root, under Python 3.12.3.

Required offline end-to-end test of the server rollup refresh: bounded and reaped build and verification workers, /proc source-holder scans, activation, containment and retention. It needs Linux and root: process groups, nice/ionice/prlimit and other processes' /proc/<pid>/fd. Run as root by .github/workflows/linux-release-build.yml, step "Server-maintenance tests", under Python 3.12.3.

Required offline test of the Python port of the source-state predicate (journals, symlinked alias, device:inode, generation marker, updater scan). It needs Linux: symlink and permission semantics and /proc. Run by .github/workflows/linux-release-build.yml, step "Server-maintenance tests", as the runner user (permission cases) and as root, under Python 3.12.3.
